output.reason: Two days of black tarry stools with lightheadedness on standing suggests ongoing upper GI bleeding with possible significant blood loss, requiring immediate emergency assessment, labs and endoscopic capability that messaging cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Black, tarry stools with lightheadedness on standing can mean active bleeding in your gut and meaningful blood loss. Have someone drive you rather than driving yourself. Call 911 instead if you faint, vomit blood or coffee-ground material, feel your heart racing, or become confused or short of breath.
differential: Upper GI bleed (e.g. peptic ulcer) causing melena
Other GI bleeding source or non-blood black stool (e.g. iron/bismuth)
